feel.neutral: Quiet, Swiss, gets out of the way
feel.editorial: Magazine confidence, opinionated serif or grotesque
feel.elegant: High contrast, refined, a little luxurious
feel.loud: Heavy, condensed or wide, poster energy
feel.retro: Clearly from an era: pixel, terminal, LCD, collegiate, medieval

use.headlines: Section titles and large text inside a page
use.posters: Hero text, covers, one-word big moments
use.accessible: Built for legibility: low vision, dyslexia, small sizes

license.OFL: SIL Open Font License: use, modify, bundle and redistribute with the license file
license.FFL: ITF Free Font License (Fontshare): free commercial use and self-hosting; never redistribute, modify, subset or convert the files

fonts.name: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next
fonts.note: Made for low-vision readers: every confusable letter (I l 1, O 0) is distinct. A humane alternative to Inter for UI.

fonts.name: Public Sans
fonts.note: The U.S. government's plain, dependable grotesque. An alternative to Inter or Roboto with less baggage.

fonts.name: Mona Sans / Hubot Sans
fonts.note: GitHub's variable grotesque with a width axis, so one family covers condensed headlines and normal UI. Hubot Sans is its squarer, more mechanical sibling.
fonts.caveats: Strongly associated with GitHub; avoid for developer-tool brands that shouldn't look like GitHub.

fonts.name: IBM Plex Sans
fonts.note: Corporate-engineered grotesque with small quirks that keep it from being bland. Pairs with Plex Serif and Plex Mono.
fonts.caveats: Separate Plex families also cover Arabic, Devanagari, Hebrew, Thai, Japanese, Korean and Chinese.

fonts.name: Red Hat Display / Text
fonts.note: Friendly geometric-humanist pair: Display for big sizes, Text for small. An alternative to Poppins or Montserrat.
fonts.caveats: Red Hat Text stops at 700; 800 and 900 are Display only.

fonts.name: Overpass
fonts.note: Based on US highway signage (Highway Gothic): open, legible, a little civic. Has a matching mono.

fonts.name: Source Sans 3
fonts.note: Adobe's calm humanist workhorse with wide language support. An alternative to Open Sans.

fonts.name: Karrik
fonts.note: A grotesque with odd notches cut into its strokes; reads as normal from afar and strange up close.
fonts.caveats: Single weight. Velvetyne's site was redirecting to a strike notice in Nov 2026; try again later or use a mirror that keeps the OFL file.

fonts.name: Sporting Grotesque
fonts.note: A wide, slightly old-fashioned grotesque with sporty swagger. Feels like a vintage club badge.
fonts.caveats: Two weights only.

fonts.name: League Spartan
fonts.by: The League of Moveable Type / Tyler Finck
fonts.note: Bold geometric in the Futura tradition; the heaviest weights are the reason to use it.
fonts.caveats: No italics.

fonts.name: Switzer
fonts.note: Classic neo-grotesque with 9 weights and true italics. The quieter, less-seen alternative to Inter and Satoshi.

fonts.name: Supreme
fonts.note: Straight-sided, monolinear engineer's grotesque. An alternative to Space Grotesk without the trend.
fonts.caveats: Italics are obliques (slanted uprights).

fonts.name: Synonym
fonts.note: Humanist sans with visible stroke contrast; personality without losing legibility. Made for branding and editorial.
fonts.caveats: No italics, so weak for long body text with emphasis.

fonts.name: Technor
fonts.note: Constructed sans with flat sides and rounded tops. Sci-fi and industrial without being a cliché.

fonts.name: Ranade
fonts.note: Neo-grotesque with high-contrast diagonals, a little kick that sets it apart from Helvetica clones.

fonts.name: Author
fonts.note: Slightly wide humanist sans made for publications. Roomy, readable, a sans that likes books.

fonts.name: Plein
fonts.note: Monolinear humanist sans with open, pleasant forms. An alternative to DM Sans.

fonts.name: Alpino
fonts.note: Magazine humanist sans: small x-height, long ascenders, oldstyle figures, softly rounded corners.
fonts.caveats: No italics. Small x-height reads small at UI sizes.

fonts.name: Source Serif 4
fonts.note: Sturdy transitional serif with an optical-size axis, so it looks right from captions to headlines.

fonts.name: IBM Plex Serif
fonts.note: A serif with an engineer's precision; pairs naturally with Plex Sans and Plex Mono.

fonts.name: Libertinus
fonts.note: Classic old-style book face with huge language coverage and a math companion. For essays, papers, long reads.

fonts.name: Cormorant
fonts.note: Delicate Garamond-style display serif with long, sharp details. Luxurious at large sizes.
fonts.caveats: Too thin for body text on screens; use Cormorant Garamond or another serif for text.

fonts.name: Junicode
fonts.note: A scholar's serif built for medievalists, with weight and width axes. Old-world without being a costume.
fonts.caveats: Very large character set for medieval and runic text; subset it for the web.

fonts.name: Bagnard
fonts.note: Based on graffiti carved by a Napoleonic-era prisoner: rough, heavy, unusual serif with real character.
fonts.caveats: Single style. Display only.

fonts.name: Avara
fonts.note: A curveless serif: every curve drawn as straight segments. Classic silhouette, faceted up close.
fonts.caveats: Bold and Black only; italic only for Bold.

fonts.name: Happy Times at the IKOB
fonts.note: A cheeky riff on Times New Roman with odd, joyful details. Times, but it smiles.

fonts.name: Sorts Mill Goudy
fonts.by: Barry Schwartz (The League of Moveable Type)
fonts.note: A revival of Goudy Oldstyle: warm, bookish, early-20th-century American printing.
fonts.caveats: Regular and italic only; no bold.

fonts.name: Linden Hill
fonts.by: Barry Schwartz (The League of Moveable Type)
fonts.note: A revival of Goudy's Deepdene: graceful, slightly calligraphic old-style serif.
fonts.caveats: Regular and italic only; no bold.

fonts.name: Gambetta
fonts.note: Text serif with diagonal stress and contrast that grows with weight. Newspaper-grade reading.

fonts.name: Zodiak
fonts.note: Sturdy Century-style serif. Middle weights set text; the extreme thin and black weights make great display pairs.

fonts.name: Erode
fonts.note: Contrasty serif with long ascenders and open counters. Made for pull quotes and eye-catching headlines.

fonts.name: Sentient
fonts.note: Slightly wide, robust serif for immersive long reading. Holds up at small sizes.

fonts.name: Gambarino
fonts.note: Condensed post-modern Garalde for headlines. Pair it with a quieter text serif or sans.
fonts.caveats: Single weight, display only.

fonts.name: Recia
fonts.note: Low-contrast, slightly condensed contemporary serif with true cursive italics. A serif that works on screens.

fonts.name: Bespoke Serif
fonts.note: Wedge-serif text face with big open counters, designed for reading.

fonts.name: Boska
fonts.note: High-contrast Didone with a pointed-pen flourish. Fashion-magazine elegance. An alternative to Playfair Display.
fonts.caveats: Hairlines break up at small sizes; headlines only.

fonts.name: Trench Slab
fonts.note: Slab serif with big, prominent ink traps that become a visible style at large sizes.
fonts.caveats: Made for larger-than-reading sizes.

fonts.name: Hoover
fonts.note: Monolinear slab with no curves at all. Pure American collegiate and varsity-jacket lettering.

fonts.name: Ouroboros
fonts.note: Looping, snake-like letterforms. Strange, organic, impossible to mistake for a template.
fonts.caveats: Single style. Display only.

fonts.name: Basteleur
fonts.note: Medieval-inspired serif with wild, sharp details; Moonlight is delicate, Bold is gothic drama.
fonts.caveats: Two styles only: Moonlight (light) and Bold.

fonts.name: Terminal Grotesque
fonts.note: Rough pixel grotesque, cyberpunk zine energy.
fonts.caveats: Single weight, plus an 'Open' variant.

fonts.name: Le Murmure
fonts.note: Tall, narrow display face with alternate letters. Made for a Paris agency; fashion-poster attitude.
fonts.caveats: Single weight.

fonts.name: Sligoil
fonts.note: Based on slug-shaped, gel-like forms; monospace-ish and alien. Ships a variable font.

fonts.name: League Gothic
fonts.note: Tall condensed gothic (an Alternate Gothic revival) with a width axis. Classic newspaper and poster shout. An alternative to Bebas Neue and Oswald.
fonts.caveats: One weight; the variable axis is width, not weight.

fonts.name: Ostrich Sans
fonts.by: Tyler Finck (The League of Moveable Type)
fonts.note: Ultra-condensed caps with rounded, inline and dashed variants. Fun, tall and skinny.
fonts.caveats: Mostly caps-only. Display only.

fonts.name: Knewave
fonts.by: Tyler Finck (The League of Moveable Type)
fonts.note: Bold brush script with skate and surf energy.
fonts.caveats: Single weight.

fonts.name: Tanker
fonts.note: Condensed caps-only sans: the lowercase keys type classic caps and the uppercase keys type dynamic, experimental ones.
fonts.caveats: Uppercase only. Single weight.

fonts.name: Panchang
fonts.note: Ultra-wide, almost panoramic sans. Industrial and very confident.
fonts.caveats: Takes a lot of horizontal space; short words only.

fonts.name: Aktura
fonts.note: Modern blackletter with ornate Lombardic capitals. Newspaper nameplate, diploma or metal band.
fonts.caveats: Single weight. Don't set all caps, the capitals are ornate.

fonts.name: Zina
fonts.note: Stately inline Didone with ball terminals. Early-1800s grandeur.
fonts.caveats: Single weight. Large sizes only, the inline disappears small.

fonts.name: Kola
fonts.note: Rounded techno stencil sans, a bit like LED signage. Large x-height keeps it readable.
fonts.caveats: Single weight.

fonts.name: Melodrama
fonts.note: Sans with extreme contrast that grows with weight. Glamorous and theatrical.
fonts.caveats: Thin strokes vanish at small sizes.

fonts.name: Segment
fonts.note: LCD-style letters built from segments. Digital clocks, transit boards, calculators.
fonts.caveats: Single weight.

fonts.name: Commit Mono
fonts.note: Neutral, anonymous coding font with smart kerning. Configurable on the site before download. An alternative to JetBrains Mono.

fonts.name: Monaspace
fonts.note: Five metric-compatible monos (Neon, Argon, Xenon, Radon, Krypton) you can mix in one editor, e.g. a handwriting-style mono for comments.

fonts.name: Departure Mono
fonts.note: Pixel monospace inspired by old computers and NASA. Charming at its native pixel sizes.
fonts.caveats: Single weight. Set at multiples of 11px to keep the pixels crisp.

fonts.name: Intel One Mono
fonts.note: Coding font designed with and for low-vision developers. Clear, open and calm.

fonts.name: iA Writer Mono / Duo / Quattro
fonts.note: Plex Mono reworked for writing. Duo and Quattro are duospace and quattrospace, so prose reads more naturally than in a true mono.

fonts.name: Recursive
fonts.note: One variable font that slides from sans to mono and from linear to casual brush. Great for friendly dev brands.
fonts.caveats: Italics come from the slant and cursive axes, not separate files.

fonts.name: Iosevka
fonts.note: Narrow, highly configurable coding font. Fits lots of columns; build your own variant.
fonts.caveats: Huge download; pick a prebuilt web package or a custom build.

fonts.name: Victor Mono
fonts.note: Narrow mono with a cursive italic. Comments and keywords look handwritten.

fonts.name: IBM Plex Mono
fonts.note: Mono with a slightly humanist italic. Works for code and for tech-flavoured UI labels.

fonts.name: Steps Mono
fonts.note: Stepped, angular mono. More art piece than coding font.
fonts.caveats: Thin and Regular only. Not for real code.

avoid.name: Inter
avoid.why: The default of nearly every AI-generated UI and SaaS template.

avoid.name: Geist
avoid.why: Vercel's font; now the default look of AI-generated Next.js apps.

avoid.name: Space Grotesk
avoid.why: The go-to 'techy but friendly' choice in templates.

avoid.name: Instrument Serif
avoid.why: The default 'tasteful serif' in AI landing pages.

avoid.name: Poppins
avoid.why: The most overused geometric sans on the web.

avoid.name: Montserrat
avoid.why: The most overused display sans on the web.

avoid.name: Roboto
avoid.why: Android and Material default; reads as 'no decision made'.

avoid.name: JetBrains Mono
avoid.why: The default mono in AI-generated code UIs.

avoid.name: Satoshi
avoid.why: Fontshare's most-used font; the default of Framer-style templates.

avoid.name: Clash Display
avoid.why: The default 'bold display' of Framer-style templates.
